title: Optimized Budget Allocation Using Multi-Criteria Decision Making and Genetic Algorithms
authors: Gulbakyt, D.; Karataev, A.; Myrzaliyev, M.; Akhmetsultanov, A.
tldr: A hybrid optimization framework combining MCDM methods (AHP, SAW, TOPSIS, WASPAS) with genetic algorithms allocates fixed budgets across competing financial goals, demonstrating genetic algorithms yield superior trade-off solutions.
problem_and_motivation: Individuals commonly allocate budgets based on intuition or routine rather than structured optimization, leading to resource misallocation and neglect of important goals. Multi-criteria optimization is mathematically intractable by exhaustive search. There is a lack of empirical validation comparing MCDM-based budgeting against non-allocation and subjective allocation across diverse financial profiles.
approach: Formulated budget allocation as a multi-objective optimization problem with satisfaction, necessity, impact, and risk as criteria.
Implemented genetic algorithm-based optimization to generate Pareto-optimal allocation plans from an extensive solution space.
Integrated AHP for weight derivation, SAW for linear scoring, TOPSIS for distance-to-ideal ranking, and WASPAS for combined weighted aggregation.
Defined four financial profiles (student, freelancer, retiree, low-income) with distinct constraints, liabilities, and income streams.
Generated 1000 alternative allocations per profile using Latin Hypercube Sampling for comparative benchmarking.
Conducted robustness analysis using Monte Carlo perturbations of AHP-derived weights.
Evaluated performance across three allocation strategies: no allocation, subjective allocation, and MCDM-based allocation.
Used non-dominated sorting to identify Pareto fronts and computed hypervolume indicator for solution quality assessment.
findings: Genetic algorithm-based allocation consistently yields superior trade-off solutions compared to SAW, TOPSIS, and WASPAS.
Budget profiles with lower liabilities exhibit greater allocation flexibility than those constrained by fixed payments.
AHP weight allocation significantly influences outcomes, particularly for profiles with high financial obligations.
The combination of AHP with WASPAS provides the most accurate and robust ranking across budget profiles.
Monte Carlo simulations reveal that objective weighting procedures introduce minor perturbations but maintain ranking robustness.
No-allocation strategy performs poorly for profiles with critical expenses such as loan repayments.
MCDM-based allocation adapts dynamically to changing financial constraints while maintaining goal satisfaction.

definitions.definition: Multi-Criteria Decision Making, a framework for evaluating alternatives against multiple conflicting criteria.
Analytic Hierarchy Process, a structured technique for deriving criteria weights through pairwise comparisons.
Simple Additive Weighting, a linear scoring method summing weighted normalized criteria values.
Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution, ranking alternatives by distance to ideal and anti-ideal points.
Weighted Aggregated Sum Product Assessment, combining weighted sum and weighted product models for robust ranking.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper contributes a structured hybrid framework for personal budget allocation that combines multi-criteria decision making (AHP, SAW, TOPSIS, WASPAS) with genetic algorithm-based optimization. It provides empirical evidence that computational optimization outperforms intuitive allocation, identifies that financial profiles with lower liabilities have greater allocation flexibility, and demonstrates that WASPAS combined with AHP yields the most robust rankings across heterogeneous financial profiles.
directly_justifies: Genetic algorithm-based allocation consistently produces superior trade-off solutions across all tested profiles.
Financial profiles with lower fixed liabilities allow greater allocation flexibility.
WASPAS with AHP provides the most accurate and robust ranking of budget alternatives.
Monte Carlo simulations confirm that AHP weight perturbations do not significantly alter ranking robustness.
No-allocation strategy performs poorly for profiles with critical financial obligations.
limits: Does not incorporate real-time user feedback or adaptive learning mechanisms.
Synthetic data from Latin Hypercube Sampling rather than empirical financial records.
Evaluation limited to four predefined financial profiles without generalization testing.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: The paper was systematically scanned across all 14 topic domains. Domain 7 (Budgeting) received high relevance as the core contribution is budget allocation optimization. Domain 4 (Existing Systems) received medium relevance for contextualizing current allocation practices. Domain 13 (Evaluation) received medium relevance for the comparative benchmarking methodology. Domain 5 (Behavioral Profiles) received medium relevance through the financial profile modeling. Domains 6, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 14 were considered and rejected as the paper does not address predictive modeling, anomaly detection, mobile design, privacy, expense categorization, evaluation frameworks, or synthetic data generation beyond budget allocation contexts.

limitations: Evaluation limited to synthetic financial profiles rather than real-world user data.
No consideration of real-time adaptation or user feedback loops.
Fixed objective criteria weights derived from AHP may not capture all individual preferences.
Does not address implementation in mobile or consumer-facing applications.
remember_this: Genetic algorithms consistently outperform SAW, TOPSIS, and WASPAS for multi-objective budget allocation.
WASPAS combined with AHP provides the most robust ranking across different financial profiles.
Financial profiles with lower liabilities have greater allocation flexibility.
Structured optimization significantly outperforms intuitive budget allocation in all tested scenarios.
Monte Carlo robustness analysis confirms minimal impact of weight perturbations on final rankings.
